newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -UNSETTLED FTSE MAY RETREAT TO 5,060.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -UNSETTLED FTSE MAY RETREAT TO 5,060.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index may retreat to around 5,060 on Friday and the prospects of a return to near the 5,100 level will have to wait, technical analysts said.
The market began to lose its form late on Thursday by backing away from 5,100, but the 187 point rally of the past four days will take its toll, they added.
Bank shares, pharmaceuticals and oils may all weaken to some extent as profit-takers make their presence known and a reactionary bounce later in the day may give way to further unsettled conditions.
By 0718 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 5.4 at 5,081.4.

A warning of the stock market's instability was given from trendlines connecting the FTSE's intra-day highs and lows since the start of the week which have been diverging as the index has made larger daily moves.

The FTSE's 10-day momentum indicator is also now at a high reading and while it is possible for this indicator to edge a little higher, such a rise will be limited over the short-term and it increases the risk of a larger fall by the FTSE later on, analysts said.
In contrast, upward momentum in Dow Jones industrials is fading so analysts forecast further weakness on Wall Street.
On Thursday the Dow closed down 71.31 at 8,188.00 taking its 10-day momentum to 71 having been as high as 300 at the start of the month.

Further gains on the Dow would lead to greater divergence between that index and its 10-day momentum and implies that a correction may be not too far off -- and this will impact the FTSE, analysts said.
The FTSE's 10-day momentum is currently at 235 -- which is close to its nearest peak level of 252 of July 14.
